definitions.explanation: A Japanese dish consisting of various ingredients skewered and deep-fried, typically served with sauce.

examples.japanese: {串揚|くしあ}げを{食|た}べに{行|い}く。
{大阪|おおさか}は{串揚|くしあ}げが{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
{串揚|くしあ}げの{店|みせ}では{二度漬|にどづ}け{禁止|きんし}がルールだ。
examples.english: At kushiage restaurants, double-dipping is against the rules.

examples.japanese: {野菜|やさい}や{肉|にく}、{海鮮|かいせん}など{様々|さまざま}な{串揚|くしあ}げを{楽|たの}しんだ。
examples.english: I enjoyed various kushiage including vegetables, meat, and seafood.

notes:
{串揚|くしあ}げ is a popular Japanese fried food.

ORIGIN:
Originated in Osaka and is a specialty of the Shinsekai district.

ALSO CALLED:
{串|くし}カツ (kushikatsu) - more common in Osaka

SERVING STYLE:
Typically served with a communal pot of sauce. The rule {二度漬|にどづ}け{禁止|きんし} (no double-dipping) is strictly followed for hygiene.

COMMON INGREDIENTS:
- {肉|にく}: meat (pork, beef)
- {野菜|やさい}: vegetables (onion, lotus root)
- {海鮮|かいせん}: seafood (shrimp, squid)
- {卵|たまご}: quail eggs
